name: How to Plan Your Kitchen Lighting Upgrade

step.name: Step 1: Assess Your Current Needs. Start by observing your kitchen throughout the day. Where are the dark spots? Do you struggle to see when cooking at the stove or countertop? Do you want to highlight certain features or create different moods? Understanding these needs will guide your lighting choices. This initial assessment might take a few days of mindful observation.

Do you want to highlight certain features or create different moods? Understanding these needs will guide your lighting choices. This initial assessment might take a few days of mindful observation.

step.name: Step 2: Understand Lighting Layers. A well-lit kitchen uses a mix of ambient, task, and accent lighting. Ambient lighting provides general illumination (e.g., recessed lights, flush mounts). Task lighting focuses on work areas (e.g., under-cabinet lights, pendants over an island). Accent lighting highlights features (e.g., track lighting aimed at artwork or shelves). Planning these layers ensures a versatile and functional space. This planning phase usually takes a few hours of research and discussion.

step.name: Step 3: Choose Fixture Types and Styles. Once you know what kind of lighting you need, you can explore fixtures. Consider recessed lighting for a clean look, pendant lights for style over an island or sink, under-cabinet lighting for task illumination, and even decorative sconces. Match the style of fixtures to your kitchen's aesthetic. Browsing options and making selections can take several days, as there are many choices.

step.name: Step 4: Plan Wiring and Switching. This is a critical step, especially if you're adding new fixtures or moving existing ones. You'll need to consider electrical capacity and the placement of switches and dimmers. Dimmers are highly recommended for flexibility. This often requires consulting with an electrician or a general contractor like Simply Construction to ensure it's done safely and up to code, usually taking a few hours for a professional assessment.

step.name: Step 5: Professional Installation. For safety and proper function, especially with new wiring or complex setups, professional installation is key. A licensed contractor ensures all electrical work meets local codes in Las Vegas, North Las Vegas, Summerlin, and surrounding areas. They can also ensure proper placement for optimal light distribution. Installation time varies depending on the scope but typically takes 1-3 days.
